Anya V: quick flag — ran the eval harness against model r1.3-quant on staging and got different outputs on two runs despite --seed=42 and identical input set. short repro below, panic because this will break CI flakiness detection
Ben L: hm, same binary and same quant kernels?
Anya V: yes. docker image sha256: a1b2c3..., quant kernels v2.4. invoked: `./eval-runner --suite wmt-small --model r1.3-quant --seed 42 --top_p 0.92 --workers 4 --batch-size 8`
Rory: curious — did you run with `--streaming-resume` or any resume path? we've seen KV cache resume interact with sharded workers before
Anya V: no resume. full cold start both times. diffing outputs: first run produced BLEU 27.3, second run 26.1. sample mismatch shows token divergence at step ~34 for some examples
Samir: can you paste the small log excerpt where it diverged?
Anya V: pasted below:
```
[2026-03-19 14:12:03] worker-2: sampling rng seed=42 init ok
[2026-03-19 14:12:03] worker-0: sampling rng seed=42 init ok
[2026-03-19 14:12:03] sampler: top_p cutoff computed at 0.92
[2026-03-19 14:12:03] worker-1: sampled token=451 at step=33
[2026-03-19 14:12:03] worker-3: sampled token=117 at step=33
[2026-03-19 14:12:03] worker-0: sampled token=451 at step=33
[2026-03-19 14:12:03] comparator: mismatch detected example=23 step=34 ref=451 run=117
```
Ben L: interesting ordering there — workers sampling same step but different tokens. maybe RNG state per worker is correct but batching/ordering changes which worker handles which example -> different token sets due to top_p being computed per-batch instead of per-example
Rory: we had a change last week to compute top_p dynamically on the active shard probabilities to avoid recomputing for every example, but that depends on the batch ordering. If worker-to-example assignment is nondeterministic across runs (due to thread scheduling) the top_p rounding can push different tails over the cutoff
Samir: that could explain it. so seeding rng isn't sufficient if top_p indexing depends on floating rounding + ordering. two mitigations: 1) make top_p selection deterministic by computing per-example, or 2) use top_k instead for evals where determinism is required
Anya V: quick test: re-run single-worker `--workers 1` and we got identical outputs across runs. multi-worker diverges.
Rory: ok that strongly points to order-dependent cutoff. can you add debug flags to log the cumulative prob thresholds per-example and per-batch? e.g. `--debug-sampling=prob_trace`
Anya V: added trace: seems small fp differences (1e-7) push some tokens above/below 0.92 when aggregated in different orders. reproducible when changing thread count to 2 as well
Ben L: then it's a numerical stability + scheduling bug. for CI we should: 1) pin `--workers=1` for determinism in regressions, or 2) change eval harness to use a deterministic sampler that enforces a fixed per-example ordering before sampling.
Rory: I'll open an infra patch to add a `--deterministic-sampling` flag which forces per-example top_p and uses a reproducible per-example RNG stream (seed combined with example id). will also add a unit test that runs with multiple workers and checks outputs identical to single-worker baseline
ci-bot: triggered re-run of failing eval job (#4521) — status: queued
Anya V: thanks. created a minimal reproducer gist and linked in the ticket: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-sampler-ordering
Samir: one more note — quantized kernels sometimes reorder softmax ops for perf; let's make sure there isn't a backend reorder that changes FP accumulation. I'll run with float32 kernels as a cross-check
Ben L: good plan. can we also log a sha256 of the token sequences per-example at the end of each run so CI can diff quickly? would make flake triage much faster
Anya V: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
Rory: assigning to eng-runtime to implement `--deterministic-sampling` and add regression test. filing a postmortem if this caused any CI churn.
ci-bot: re-run started for job #4521 (deterministic-sampling test disabled)
